persona.name: Alex
persona.description: Alex studies the biology, systematics, and ecology of butterflies and curates a collection of Lepidoptera specimens. His research focuses on the monitoring, taxonomy, and conservation of European butterflies, particularly those from the Macaronesian Islands. He frequently works with type specimens to verify species identities, investigate taxonomic relationships, and analyze biodiversity patterns.

scenario_and_motivation.scenario: Alex regularly consults type specimens and their associated metadata to support taxonomic, ecological, and conservation research. Currently, much of this information is scattered across specimen labels, publications, collection databases, and PDF catalogs, making searches time-consuming and inefficient.
scenario_and_motivation.motivation: A Type Specimen Knowledge Base would provide centralized, structured access to information on type specimens.
benefits: Verify whether a newly recognized species has previously been described under another name.
Identify the institution or collection where a type specimen is deposited.
Access linked resources such as photographs, DNA barcodes, and related publications.
Analyze trends in species discovery and description over time.
Explore the geographic distribution and provenance of type specimens.

user_story.title: Chief Editor of a Zoological Journal

persona.name: Maria
persona.description: Maria is responsible for the scientific content, quality, and strategic development of a zoological journal with a focus on insects. She works to increase the visibility, dissemination, and impact of the journal while supporting the mission of the research institute that hosts it as a diamond open-access publication. Maria advocates for open access, open data, FAIR principles, and the data liberation approach outlined in the Disentis Roadmap. She seeks to make type specimen information published in the journal accessible, discoverable, and reusable in order to strengthen the journal’s contribution to biodiversity research and the open science ecosystem.

scenario_and_motivation.scenario: Maria wants a comprehensive overview of the type specimen information published in her journal and better insight into the journal’s contribution to biodiversity knowledge. Currently, information about type specimens is embedded within publications and cannot easily be retrieved, aggregated, or analyzed. Answering questions about the journal’s type specimen content often requires manual searches, OCR processing, and spreadsheet compilation.
scenario_and_motivation.motivation: A Type Specimen Knowledge Base would provide structured and machine-readable access to type specimen information published in the journal. It would increase the visibility, discoverability, and reuse of these data, support reporting and strategic planning, and help demonstrate the journal’s scientific contribution and impact.
knowledge_base_should_support: Centralized access to type specimen information published in the journal
Discovery of type specimen records through biodiversity infrastructures and external knowledge systems
Reporting to institute management, advisory boards, and editorial boards
Monitoring trends in publication of type specimen information
Identification of key publications and collections contributing to scientific impact
benefits: Obtain a comprehensive overview of all type specimens published or mentioned in the journal.
Demonstrate the journal’s contribution to biodiversity knowledge and taxonomy.
Increase the visibility, discoverability, and reuse of type specimen information.
Support reporting activities for institute management, advisory boards, and the editorial board.
Monitor trends and developments in the publication of type specimen information.
Identify key publications and collections contributing to the journal’s scientific impact.
Strengthen the reputation of the journal and attract authors publishing high-quality research.
Support open science principles by making published data more FAIR and reusable.

persona.name: Thomas
persona.description: Thomas is responsible for the operational management, documentation, and quality assurance of an entomological collection. He maintains and develops collection management systems, coordinates digitization activities, and ensures that specimen information is accurate, complete, and accessible. He works with curators, collection scientists, collection managers, and researchers to integrate information from collection databases, historical catalogues, scientific publications, archives, and specimen labels.

scenario_and_motivation.scenario: Thomas wants to improve the quality, completeness, and accessibility of information about specimens held in his collection. Type specimen information is often distributed across collection management systems, historical catalogues, scientific publications, archives, and specimen labels, making it difficult to maintain complete and consistent collection records.
scenario_and_motivation.motivation: A Type Specimen Knowledge Base would provide structured access to information contained in type specimen catalogues and publications and allow Thomas to connect it with existing collection documentation. It would support record enrichment, metadata quality improvement, inconsistency detection, and access to historical documentation and expert knowledge.
knowledge_base_should_support: Integration of information from catalogues, publications, collection databases, archives, and specimen labels
Enrichment of specimen records with additional metadata and identifiers
Verification and reconciliation of information from different sources
Identification of missing, incomplete, or inconsistent specimen information
Links between physical specimens, digital records, and published scientific knowledge
Data quality assurance and digitization activities
benefits: Identify information contained in catalogues and publications that is not yet represented in collection management systems.
Enrich specimen records with additional metadata, identifiers, taxonomic information, locality information, and links to publications and external resources.
Verify and reconcile information from different sources.
Identify missing, incomplete, or inconsistent specimen information.
Strengthen the connections between physical specimens, collection records, and published scientific knowledge.
Support data quality assurance and collection digitization activities.
Improve the completeness, consistency, and accessibility of collection data.
Increase the value, usability, and discoverability of the collection for researchers, collection staff, and biodiversity knowledge infrastructures.

persona.name: Wanja
persona.description: Wanja oversees the scientific quality, strategic development, and long-term management of an entomological collection. He is responsible for ensuring the collection’s scientific relevance, documenting its strengths, and supporting research activities. His work focuses on understanding the significance, development, and knowledge value of type specimen holdings across the collection.

scenario_and_motivation.scenario: Wanja requires a comprehensive understanding of the collection’s type specimens and their scientific importance. Information about type specimens, catalogues, taxonomic coverage, specialists, and historical interpretations is often distributed across collection databases, publications, archival records, and specimen documentation, making strategic assessment difficult and time-consuming.
scenario_and_motivation.motivation: A Type Specimen Knowledge Base would provide centralized, structured access to information about type specimens, catalogues, taxonomic groups, geographic coverage, historical documentation, and collection development. Advanced search and analytical capabilities would support strategic assessment, collection planning, and research prioritization.
knowledge_base_should_support: Centralized access to type specimen information
Analysis of taxonomic and geographic coverage
Assessment of collection strengths and knowledge gaps
Access to published catalogues and collection documentation
Identification of specialists and their contributions
Support for strategic planning, digitization, and research activities
benefits: Obtain a complete overview of documented type specimens in the collection.
Assess the taxonomic and geographic coverage of type holdings.
Identify the strongest and most comprehensively represented groups.
Explore the historical development of the collection and its scientific interpretation.
Review published catalogues and their contributions to collection knowledge.
Identify specialists who have documented and studied the collection.
Support strategic decisions regarding collection development, digitization, and research priorities.
